changes.current_line: Customers see an average uplift in authorization rates with Authorization Boost and Adaptive Acceptance.
changes.change: When the buyer can give us their own failure rate, open on it and price it instead of quoting an average: 'You told us about one in twelve online orders fails at the payment step, worse on the big baskets. Here is what those orders are worth to you, and how much of it we expect to recover.' Keep the average uplift and the Authorization Boost and Adaptive Acceptance names as the explanation underneath, not the headline.
changes.why: We showed the generic uplift slide and the CFO still concluded it was 'the same thing', while the champion had already given us a measurable failure rate 'Off their own dashboard' that we never priced.

changes.change: Add a standard proof asset: a one-page business case the champion can hand a CFO who won't meet vendors. Build it from a three-month decline export and show the failed orders, what they were worth, and the total cost against the incumbent. Send it before the pricing proposal goes to finance, so the decision page shows revenue recovered and not only rate against rate.
changes.why: Lucy asked for 'something she could hand Martin. Like a one-page business case' and got the deck and pricing, so the controller's side-by-side of 'Our rate, their rate' became the only page in the room.

changes.change: Add a counter-line for when an incumbent responds with only a rate cut: 'A better rate on the same failed orders is still the same failed orders. The bank lowered what you pay per transaction. It didn't change how many of your orders die at the last step.' Use it to bring the conversation back to declines as soon as the incumbent counters on rate.
changes.why: Once the bank 'came back and sharpened the rate', with 'No new product, nothing', every email after that was about rate, even though Lucy had been asking about declines up to then.

changes.change: For ecommerce buyers with high-value online orders, lead with the champion's language and not ours: 'orders dying at the last step' and 'the big baskets', for example 'you do all the work to get someone to buy a four-thousand-dollar greenhouse and then the card says no.' Keep 'authorization rate' and 'acceptance' as the technical explanation that follows.
changes.why: The champion described the problem as lost sales and wasted effort in sharper words than our 'declines' and 'acceptance', and our terms never reached the CFO as a difference.
